title: Fix Wi-Fi dying after suspend on BCM43602 MacBooks
author: garethevs3
body:
## Summary

- `brcmfmac`'s firmware on BCM43602 (2015-2017 MacBooks) occasionally fails to reinitialize its message ring after suspend/resume: every wifi ioctl times out (`brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout on response for query command`, cascading into `-5`/`-12` errors) and Wi-Fi stays dead until a reboot.
- It's intermittent by nature — the in-place PCIe resume path sometimes succeeds and sometimes doesn't — which is why it reads as "Wi-Fi randomly dies after sleep" rather than a consistent failure. Tracked upstream and unfixed since 2017: [kernel.org bugzilla #196019](https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=196019), [#197977](https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=197977).
- Adds `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-suspend.sh`, which installs a `systemd-sleep` hook that unloads and reloads the `brcmfmac` module around every suspend, forcing the same clean firmware download a cold boot already performs successfully, instead of relying on the flaky in-place resume path.
- Scoped to the confirmed BCM43602 PCI IDs already used by `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh` (`14e4:43ba/43bb/43bc`), not the broader chip list in that file — the 2018+ and T2-era chips have different suspend behavior and are already being tracked separately in #4695.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified on a MacBookPro12,1 (BCM43602, `14e4:43ba`): observed the actual failure in `journalctl` after a real sleep/wake cycle (firmware timeout cascade, requiring a reboot to recover).
- [x] Confirmed the fix manually: repeated `pre`/`post` invocations of the installed hook complete cleanly, the `wlp3s0` interface reappears, and NetworkManager reconnects within a few seconds each time.
- [ ] Not yet verified on other BCM43602 Mac models (MacBookPro13,x) — PCI ID match should be equivalent, but flagging for anyone who can confirm.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_017XWKvdTCkjZXrGHPvDySZ4

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@
+# BCM43602's brcmfmac firmware occasionally fails to reinitialize its message
+# ring after suspend/resume: every ioctl times out ("brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd:
+# Timeout on response for query command", then cascading -5/-12 errors) and
+# Wi-Fi stays dead until a reboot. It isn't every cycle -- the driver
+# sometimes redoes the firmware download cleanly on resume and sometimes
+# doesn't -- which is what makes it read as "Wi-Fi randomly dies after
+# sleep" rather than a hard failure. See kernel.org bugzilla #196019 and
+# #197977, both open since 2017 with no upstream driver fix.
+#
+# Forcing a full module unload/reload around every suspend makes the driver
+# redo the firmware download it already performs successfully on a cold
+# boot, instead of relying on the in-place PCIe resume path that
+# intermittently fails.
+#
+# Same chip family as the four-way-handshake quirk in
+# fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh: BCM43602 and its single-band variants in
+# 2015-2017 Macs (14e4:43ba/43bb/43bc). Scoped to just that family for now --
+# the 2018+ chips (BCM4350/4355/4364) and T2-era chips (BCM4377/4378/4387)
+# have their own suspend behavior and are already being tracked separately
+# (see github.com/basecamp/omarchy/discussions/4695).
+if lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43ba|43bb|43bc)" >/dev/null; then
+  echo "Detected BCM43602 Wi-Fi; installing suspend/resume firmware-reload workaround"
+
+  mkdir -p /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep
+  cat > /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/brcmfmac-suspend.sh <<'EOF'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# Work around a brcmfmac/BCM43602 firmware bug where suspend/resume
+# occasionally leaves the wifi message ring uninitialized. See
+# install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-suspend.sh for the full explanation.
+
+case "$1" in
+  pre)
+    modprobe -r brcmfmac_wcc 2>/dev/null
+    modprobe -r brcmfmac 2>/dev/null
+    ;;
+  post)
+    modprobe brcmfmac
+    modprobe brcmfmac_wcc 2>/dev/null
+    ;;
+esac
+
+exit 0
+EOF
+  chmod 755 /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/brcmfmac-suspend.sh
+fi

comments.body:
Verified on MacBookPro11,5 (BCM43602 14e4:43ba, second model after the author's 12,1).

Repro: a suspend/resume produced the exact reported signature -- brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd timeouts cascading into -5 errors with bus is down -- and Wi-Fi stayed dead until reboot. (Disclosure: this box runs with amdgpu/radeon blacklisted for an unrelated suspend workaround; the wifi device path and the log signature match your 12,1 line-for-line.)

Fix check: installed the hook; manual pre unloads both modules and post brings the interface back. Then a systemctl suspend: a third firmware download in the journal proves the post hook fired, reconnect completed ~5s after wake, zero timeouts since.

One note on method: an rtcwake -m mem retest does NOT exercise this hook -- rtcwake bypasses systemd-sleep, confirmed by counting firmware loads. Worth naming systemctl suspend in the test plan.

Follow-up from two lid-close cycles on the same 11,5: the hook has a silent-failure mode worth hardening before merge.

Both cycles resumed cleanly, then Wi-Fi died with NO timeout cascade and NO wpa lines at all -- just silence, followed by NM wedged unkillably and a hard poweroff (plus the now-familiar frozen first reboot). Firmware-load count for the whole boot was 1 (boot only): the post never reloaded because there was nothing to reload -- the pre removal must have failed silently.

Why it fails only sometimes: the pre runs modprobe -r while NM is concurrently tearing the device down (my log shows deactivating/DHCP-cancel/inetaddr err:-52 in the same second). Twice today the identical command succeeded from an idle shell, so it is a race, hidden by 2>/dev/null. When removal loses, post modprobe is a no-op on the still-loaded module, protection is zero, and nothing logs it.

Suggestion: bring the interface down before rmmod (ip link set down on the wlp netdev), retry briefly, and fail loudly to the journal instead of 2>/dev/null -- a hook that silently no-ops leaves exactly the corpse above. Happy to test a v2 here.

Incident from the same 11,5 that sharpens the hardening note: when the firmware is already flaking as pre runs (a msgbuf timeout 2s earlier), the unload itself walked into a GPF -- brcmf_pcie_remove -> brcmf_detach -> general protection fault in _cfg80211_unregister_wdev on a 0xdead address, segfaulting modprobe and wedging wpa_supplicant into D. Suspend aborted on the unfreezable task; the screen then blanked via DPMS ~30s later, which reads exactly like dead resume but the machine never slept. The logger line is what made this diagnosable after the fact, so the loud-failure part of the suggestion is validated. Open question for the hook design: whether to attempt unload at all when the firmware is already timing out, versus logging and leaving the doomed stack alone.
Can confirm my fix is still working after a week of solid use. Haven't experienced a dropout since 👍

Lid-path proof on the 11,5, complementing the systemctl test: lid close with the v2 hook armed, firmware reload logged on resume, reconnect in 4s, zero timeouts across the cycle. The unload path fires correctly from the real lid path, not just manual invocation.

Suggested hardening for the hook, running live on my 11,5 for two clean lid cycles (one genuine unload+reload with 4s reconnect, one correct stand-down on a real timeout with clean in-place resume after). Two changes over the PR version: interface down before rmmod with a 5x retry (the plain rmmod loses a race with NM mid-teardown and fails silently), and a health gate that skips the unload when firmware timeouts are already firing -- unloading then walked into a GPF in cfg80211 unregister (use-after-free on 0xdead), segfaulting modprobe and wedging wpa_supplicant into D. Note the gate reads journalctl -b -k (kernel facility only): without -k, sudo's own audit echo of the script text false-triggers it. Full file for adopt-as-wanted:

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Work around a brcmfmac/BCM43602 firmware bug where suspend/resume
# occasionally leaves the wifi message ring uninitialized (upstream #10332).
# Local hardening: the plain modprobe -r raced NetworkManager mid-teardown
# and failed silently, and worse, unloading while the firmware is already
# timing out wedges the stack (GPF in cfg80211 unregister, D-state tasks,
# aborted suspend). So: bring the interface down first, retry the unload,
# say so in the journal on any failure -- and skip the unload entirely when
# timeouts are already firing.

firmware_flaking() {
  journalctl -b -k --no-pager --since "5 minutes ago" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout"
}

wifi_iface() {
  local d
  for d in /sys/class/net/wl*; do
    [[ -e $d ]] && basename "$d" && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

case "$1" in
  pre)
    if firmware_flaking; then
      logger -t brcmfmac-suspend "pre: firmware timeouts firing, leaving module loaded to avoid wedging suspend"
    else
      iface=$(wifi_iface) || true
      [[ -n ${iface:-} ]] && ip link set "$iface" down 2>/dev/null || true
      for _ in 1 2 3 4 5; do
        modprobe -r brcmfmac_wcc 2>/dev/null
        modprobe -r brcmfmac 2>/dev/null && break
        sleep 1
      done
      if lsmod | grep -q "^brcmfmac "; then
        logger -t brcmfmac-suspend "pre: module still loaded after retries, resume may fail"
      fi
    fi
    ;;
  post)
    modprobe brcmfmac
    modprobe brcmfmac_wcc 2>/dev/null || true
    ;;
esac

exit 0
```

Third BCM43602 model, same signature: **MacBookPro14,2**, `14e4:43ba`, Omarchy **4.0.3-1** (the sleep hook is **not** installed here), kernel 7.2.3-arch1-3.

Lid-close S3 ~8 min, undocked. On resume:

```
ieee80211 phy13: brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout on response for query command
ieee80211 phy13: _brcmf_set_multicast_list: Setting mcast_list failed, -5
ieee80211 phy13: brcmf_c_set_cur_etheraddr: Setting cur_etheraddr failed, -5
```

NetworkManager: `do-change-link: failure 5 (Input/output error)`, could not set MAC, then `Couldn't initialize supplicant interface: Timeout was reached` four times. Interface never reached `activated` again. Full shutdown/reboot recovered.

An earlier resume the same boot had already reloaded firmware (`wlan0` renamed to `wlp2s0`, `brcmf_inetaddr_changed: fail to get arp ip table err:-52`). `feature_disable=0x82000` is present (handshake quirk); it does not cover this S3 hang.

Does not exercise the hook — 4.0.3 does not ship it. Confirms the 12,1 / 11,5 timeout cascade on 14,2 via the real lid path. Happy to test the hook (including the v2 interface-down / timeout-gate hardening) if useful.

Related but separate: T1 Touch Bar stayed dark on the same resume ([t1bridge#18](https://github.com/standardagents/t1bridge/issues/18)); not a brcmfmac problem.

A fourth BCM43602 model with the same signature, and one consequence of the bug I have not seen quantified here.

**Machine.** MacBookPro14,3 (15-inch 2017), BCM43602 `14e4:43ba`, Apple subsystem `106b:0173`, Omarchy on kernel `7.2.5-3-omarchy`. The hook from this PR is **not** installed here.

**Same failure.** Lid closed 23:54, first suspend clean. Something woke the machine 26 minutes later; the resume itself completed, and two seconds after it the firmware stopped answering:

```
00:20:42  PM: suspend exit
00:20:44  brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout on response for query command
00:20:44  _brcmf_set_multicast_list: Setting mcast_list failed, -5
```

**What it costs when the lid simply stays shut.** The reports above are short cycles — 8 minutes, a couple of lid closes. This one was left closed overnight, and because the lid is closed, logind re-requests suspend roughly every 30 seconds and hits the dead card every time:

| | |
|---|---|
| `PM: suspend entry` | 2800 |
| `brcmf_pcie_pm_enter_D3 ... returns -5` | 2797 |
| `Failed to put system to sleep ... Input/output error` | 1399 |
| first → last failure | 00:21:36 → 12:18:25, **11 h 56 min** |

So the machine never slept again all night. It was on AC here (no disconnect logged), so I cannot report a battery figure — on battery this is a flat discharge with the lid shut. Shutdown afterwards also hung: `brcmf_cfg80211_set_power_mgmt: Unable to set pm timeout, (-12)`, then the reboot stopped progressing once journald was down and needed a power cycle.

That turns "Wi-Fi is dead until reboot" into "the laptop also runs warm in a bag until morning", which seems worth having in the PR's own case for merging.

**The unload path is clean on 7.2.5.** Since this fix depends on it, and a GPF in `brcmf_pcie_remove` was reported above:

```
modprobe -r brcmfmac_wcc && modprobe -r brcmfmac && modprobe brcmfmac
```

Interface returns and reassociates in 7 s, nothing in dmesg beyond the expected teardown noise. Tested with the firmware *healthy*, which is the common case this hook runs in — not the flaking case where the GPF was seen.

**One design note, not an objection.** I went the other way here: a handler on `OnFailure=` of `systemd-suspend.service` that reloads the module only after a failed suspend, gated on `brcmf_pcie_pm_enter_D3 ... returns -5` appearing in the kernel log within the last three minutes. Trade-off against this PR's approach, stated fairly:

- unloading on *every* suspend pays the reconnect cost each time and walks the `brcmf_pcie_remove` path each time — which is where the GPF above was hit;
- acting only on failure leaves the first suspend of an incident broken, and lands on that same path when the firmware is already flaking, so it does not dodge the hazard, only meets it less often.

Preventive is the better fit for a shipped default. Mentioning it because the failure-gated shape may be useful as hardening: it gives a place to stand down when the reload itself fails, instead of repeating it.

reviews.body:
Approved. Verified the technical claims independently.

**Mechanism checks out.** The failure model is real and accurately described — kernel bugzilla [#197977](https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=197977) is literally titled `brcmf_msgbuf_query_dcmd: Timeout on response for query command`, and both cited bugs are open against BCM43602. Unload/reload around suspend via a `systemd-sleep` hook is the established workaround class for brcmfmac resume failures, and `/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep` is the correct vendor location.

**Module handling is correct across kernel generations.** On kernels ≥ 6.1 the vendor code builds as a separate `brcmfmac-wcc` module that `brcmfmac` depends on, so unloading the core first would fail with EBUSY — the script removes `brcmfmac_wcc` before `brcmfmac`, which is the right order, and the silenced errors make it a clean no-op on older kernels. Arch builds `CONFIG_BRCMFMAC_PCIE=y` as a bool compiled into `brcmfmac.ko` (not a separate transport module), so there is nothing else that needs unloading. Reloading also re-reads `/etc/modprobe.d`, so this composes correctly with `fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh`'s `feature_disable` option.

**Repo conventions.** 100644 mode matches its siblings and works because `run_logged` sources scripts with `bash -eE`; the script is `set -e`-safe (the only failure-capable commands are inside the `if` condition). The hook has a shebang, 755 mode, and `exit 0` so a hook failure can never block suspend. The lspci gate is a no-op on non-matching hardware, so adding it unconditionally to `all.sh` is safe.

**Two non-blocking notes**

1. Existing installs never see this: `install/hardware/all.sh` runs at install time only. A BCM43602 user who installed Omarchy before this lands keeps dying wifi through every update unless they rerun the script manually. The migrations mechanism exists for exactly this kind of state repair, and this script is idempotent by construction. Was a migration considered, or is install-time-only intentional for now?
2. Unlike the supplicant script, the lspci gate is not Apple-scoped (`sys_vendor` check absent). BCM43602 also ships in a few third-party PCIe cards. The workaround is benign there (one extra module cycle per suspend), so I do not think it needs the gate, just flagging the difference.

The PR's own open item (MacBookPro13,x unverified) is fair to leave for whoever owns that hardware.
